words: walk; run; hop; gallop; slide; stop; go; light feet
notes: First traveling patterns in a clear space: walk, run, hop, gallop and slide, with a freeze on the stop signal. Cues: light feet, eyes up, stop on the signal. Works toward S1.2.1, which grade 1 owns once the ways are varied while tracking space, effort and people. Assessed by a skill task: the teacher watches each child in rotating groups and marks the stop signal and one cue as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: moving all at once only after the clear space is shown (arm's length all round); no racing.

words: jump; land; bend; knees; soft; both feet
notes: Jump from two feet in a fixed spot and land softly on two feet with knees bent, then jump over a line, a flat rope or a small hoop. Introduces the cue words idea: a skill is said in two or three short cue words ('bend, swing, land soft'). Boundary: a fixed spot with nothing changing around the child; moving and changing settings come later. Assessed by a skill task: the cue 'land soft on two feet' watched once at the start of the unit and again at the check. Teacher note: soft floor or mat, no jumping from heights, shoes tied.

words: balance; still; hold; body part; wide; tall
notes: Hold a still balance on different body parts (two feet, one foot, hands and feet, knees) for a count of three, on a floor or line, with nothing changing around the child. Cues: eyes on a spot, stand tall, hold still. Boundary: still balance only; moving across a beam or bench is later. Assessed by a skill task: holds three shapes for three counts, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: bend; stretch; twist; curl; swing; my space
notes: In-place movements in a personal space: bend, stretch, twist, curl, swing and shake, fast and slow, high and low, while staying inside the personal space and keeping aware of others around. Cue: stay in your bubble. Assessed by a skill task: moves four ways in place without bumping a neighbor, watched in rotating groups.

words: roll; target; push; low; aim; partner
notes: Roll a ball along the floor to a partner or a target from a fixed spot, with a low swing and a push. Cues: look at the target, swing low, let go. Tried several ways (sitting, standing, to a wall, between two cones). Assessed by a skill task: rolls to a target two to three meters away, watched against the cue 'swing low'.

words: catch; toss; scarf; hands; eyes; hug
notes: Catch several soft objects from a fixed spot: a scarf, a balloon, a ball bounced to the child, then a gentle toss from a partner two steps away. Cues: eyes on it, hands out, hug it. Boundary: self-toss and gentle partner toss only; catching while moving is later. Assessed by a skill task: catches two of three soft tosses with the cue 'hands out', marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: soft or large balls only; no throwing at faces.

words: kick; step; ball; target; swing; foot
notes: Kick a still ball with the laces or the inside of the foot to a wall, a wide goal or a partner, from a fixed spot. Cues: look at the ball, step beside it, swing the leg through. Boundary: a still ball; a rolling ball and moving while kicking are later. Assessed by a skill task: kicks a still ball forward with a swing through, watched against two cues.

words: tap; dribble; inside of foot; control; small touches
notes: Foot dribbling as small taps of a ball with the inside of the foot while staying in one personal space, then a few steps forward. The tool's tables first expect foot dribbling in kindergarten (from the tool). Cues: small taps, ball close. Assessed by a skill task: ten taps in place with the ball staying inside the bubble, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: strike; paddle; balloon; hit; tee; swing
notes: Strike a balloon, a soft ball on a cone or a self-dropped soft ball with a short paddle or a plastic bat, from a fixed spot. Cues: eyes on it, side to the target, swing through. Boundary: a held or still object or a self-toss; a pitched ball is later. Assessed by a skill task: contacts a ball on a tee with a swing through, three of five tries. Teacher note: clear a full swing's space on every side before anyone swings; one swinger at a time per space.

words: bounce; toss; underhand; rope; hop over
notes: Early tries only, not an owned pattern: two-hand bounce and catch, then repeated hand bounces with teacher support; an underhand toss to a big target; hopping over a still rope on the floor and over a rope the teacher swings slowly, then a first self-turned rope with teacher support. Continuous bouncing (owned in grade 1, g1-bounce) and the self-turned rope (owned in grade 2, g2-rope-fixed) are attempted only, with growth marked and no number of repetitions required (rule 3 in the PE standard note). Cue: look, swing low, toss. Assessed by a skill task: one try of each, marked met, partly or not yet on one cue each (look, swing low, toss), watched at the first try and again at the check, as growth.

words: space; my space; open; near; far; bubble
notes: Know how much space is yours (an arm's length all round) and where to go in open space. Introduces the safe-space picture: a bubble around me, one direction for throwing, a look before I move. Practiced in freeze games and in moving between spots. Assessed by a knowledge task: shows with arms the size of a personal space and moves to an open spot on a signal.

words: fitness; strong; heart; run; climb; jump; play
notes: Name activities that make the body strong and keep the heart healthy (running, jumping, climbing, dancing, swimming) and sort them from sitting activities in a picture sort. Assessed by a knowledge task: names three activities that build fitness. Fitness is a word and a habit here, never a score.

words: breathe; hot; tired; fast; slow; heart; easy; hard
notes: Notice what changes in the body during and after moving: breathing gets faster, the face feels warm, the heart beats harder. Introduces the effort scale as three faces, easy, medium and hard, chosen after resting, walking and running. Assessed by a knowledge task: chooses a face after two kinds of movement and says one body change. Teacher note: a child who prefers not to run can still show effort by another movement.

words: turn; share; listen; please; stop signal; thank you
notes: Use short phrases to share space and equipment ('my turn, your turn', 'may I use it?') and respond to the teacher's start and stop signals and feedback. Assessed by conduct, marked once in the unit against the stated behaviors: takes turns, stops on the signal, listens to the cue.

words: equipment; carry; gentle; careful; put back
notes: Handle and use gym equipment safely: carry with two hands, put it down gently, use it only in its own way, and put it back. Assessed by conduct: following three stated equipment rules during stations. Teacher note: teacher checks equipment before class; no equipment thrown at people.

words: dance; happy; calm; tired; proud; feel
notes: Name movement activities where a child can show feelings (animal walks, scarf dance, moving to a slow and a fast song) and name ways moving helps them feel well (more energy, calmer after moving, a strong heart from kindergarten's fitness unit). Assessed by a knowledge task: names one activity and one feeling, and two ways moving helps them feel well. No right answers; the point is to connect movement and feeling.

words: choose; station; chance; try; again
notes: See chances to be active during PE class: choosing a station, a partner task or a free-movement minute, and trying again after a miss. Introduces the first step of a goal: pick one thing to try today. Assessed by conduct: picks a station and keeps trying for the time given.

words: skip; run; gallop; pathway; direction; speed; forward; sideways
notes: Travel in several ways (walk, run, hop, gallop, slide, skip) and change pathway, direction and speed while keeping track of space, effort and others. Cues: eyes up, light feet, change on the signal. Owns S1.2.1 in grade 1, where the patterns are first shown across changing settings. Assessed by a skill task: travels three ways around cones and other children without bumping, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: weight; shift; hands; feet; knees; shoulders; transfer
notes: Shift weight onto different body parts (feet to hands to knees to back) in a space with a soft floor, and move from one balance to another. Weight transfer is first expected in grade 1 (from the tool). Cues: slow, keep weight in the middle, soft hands. Assessed by a skill task: moves smoothly between three weight-bearing shapes. Teacher note: mats for hands-down work; no headstands or inversions.

words: bounce; dribble; push down; waist; finger pads
notes: Bounce a ball in several in-place tasks: two hands, one hand, to a partner, to a wall and back. Cues: push the ball, fingers wide, eyes up. Boundary: in place only; dribbling on the move is a grade 3 skill. Assessed by a skill task: five bounces in a row with one hand, watched against two cues. Hand dribbling is first expected in kindergarten in the review tool; owned here (ours, untested).

words: strike; palm; balloon; volley; keep it up
notes: Hit a balloon or a light ball upward with the hand, the palm or the arm (keep it up), alone and with a partner, from a fixed spot. Cues: eyes on the ball, flat hand, hit up. Assessed by a skill task: keeps a balloon up three times in a row with a flat hand. Teacher note: balloon allergy check; use a soft ball if needed.

words: dance; rhythm; beat; step; clap; folk dance
notes: Do traveling, in-place and object-handling moves taken from a few dance styles (a circle dance, a line dance, a scarf or ribbon dance): step to the beat, turn, clap, slide. Cues: listen to the beat, follow the leader. Dance styles come from many cultures. Assessed by a skill task: moves to the beat in a simple pattern. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: jump; balance; rope; swing; hop
notes: Uses jumps and balances in new settings (jump over a low rope, land and hold a balance) and a first self-turned rope with no jumping, only swinging it. Self-turned rope in a fixed spot is owned in grade 2. Assessed by a skill task: jumps a still rope and holds the landing for two counts.

words: roll; catch; throw; underhand; partner; target
notes: Rolls, catches and underhand throws in partner and target tasks, a step to a partner and back. Work toward the overhand throw: face the target, throw underhand with the opposite foot forward. Cues: look, step, swing low. Assessed by a skill task: underhand toss to a partner three of five tries. Overhand throwing is owned in grade 2.

words: kick; dribble; paddle; strike; tee
notes: Kicking, foot tapping and short-tool striking used in new settings: a kick at a moving-in-place target, a tap and a few steps, a hit off a tee into open space. Cues from kindergarten stay on the card. Assessed by a skill task: one watched try of each. Teacher note: swing space and kick direction stay clear and set by the teacher.

words: high; low; fast; slow; straight; curvy; forward; backward
notes: Name key ideas behind traveling, staying in place and handling objects: level (high, low), speed (fast, slow), pathway (straight, curvy, zigzag) and direction. Used to say what a movement is doing. Assessed by a knowledge task: names the idea in a movement the teacher shows.

words: beat; fast; slow; high; low; shape
notes: Show understanding of in-place and traveling movement ideas in dance and rhythm: move to a fast and to a slow beat, show high and low shapes, change direction on a signal. Assessed by a knowledge task shown by moving: changes speed when the music changes.

words: heart; muscle; pulse; beat; healthy; strong
notes: The heart is a muscle that gets stronger with exercise, and being active often is good for health. Introduces pulse-check: a hand on the chest, counting beats for ten seconds after resting and after running, and choosing a face from the effort scale. Assessed by a knowledge task: says that the heart is a muscle and shows where the beat is felt. Teacher note: a child who cannot find a pulse still takes part by feeling breath; counts are never compared across children.

words: kind; cheer; encourage; feel; thumbs up; helper
notes: Notice how classmates feel during play (happy, worried, left out), cheer and encourage them with kind words, and act kindly so moving together stays positive. Assessed by conduct: uses an encouraging word or gesture in partner and group tasks.

words: game; country; family; tradition; play
notes: Name and play movement games and dances from different cultures (a tag game from one place, a clapping game from another, a folk dance), with each one named by where people play it. Assessed by a knowledge task: names one game and one place. Cultural claims are checked against a source before a unit names them. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: favorite; together; partner; team; alone
notes: Point out movement activities that let a child be with others and pick favorites that fit what the child likes. Assessed by a knowledge task: names a favorite and says whether it is alone or with others. Social interaction is first expected in grade 3 in the review tool, so this stays at naming a favorite and whether it is alone or with others.

words: good at; practice; star; wish; improve
notes: Notice what the child does well in movement and where more practice would help, with a 'star and wish' pair after a skill day. Assessed by a knowledge task: names one star and one wish on a picture card. Feeds the first goals in grade 2.

words: calm; breathe; count; slow; belly; settle
notes: Use calming steps, such as slow breaths or counting to five, to manage feelings and behavior during activity (after a miss, after a bump, when excited). The steps are SEL's calm-down steps in SEL's words ('stop, breathe', the balloon breath, count to five; SEL K to 2 units 2 and 8), taken in by retrieval; PE's calm-steps card shows those same pictures for use while moving, so a child meets one card. Assessed by conduct: uses a calm step when a teacher names a hard moment. Teacher note: calm steps are offered, never a punishment. Teacher note on emotions: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: overhand; throw; side to target; opposite foot; follow through
notes: Owns throwing in grade 2: the overhand throw as a pattern with key parts, in several in-place tasks (to a wall, a partner, a target). Cues: side to the target, step with the opposite foot, follow through. Overhand is worked toward in kindergarten and grade 1. Assessed by a skill task: three throws watched against the three cues, marked per cue. Teacher note: one throwing direction for everyone; soft balls; no human targets. Overhand is first expected in grade 2 (from the review tool).

words: long bat; swing; level swing; tee; side to target
notes: Hit a ball from a tee or a self-drop with a long-handled tool (plastic bat, hockey stick, golf-style club) in several in-place tasks. Long tools are first expected in grade 2 (from the tool). Cues: side to the target, eyes on the ball, level swing. Assessed by a skill task: contacts a ball on a tee with a level swing. Teacher note: full swing space cleared; one swinger per space; stand beside, never in front.

words: rope; turn; jump; swing; rhythm; wrist
notes: Jump a self-turned rope in a fixed spot: swing a rope, jump once, then several in a row, or use a long rope with the teacher. Cues: turn from the wrists, small jumps, soft landing. Assessed by a skill task: jumps a self-turned rope three times in a row, or a long rope once with a turner. Teacher note: rope length matched to the child; soft floor. Rope is first expected in kindergarten in the review tool; owned here because a self-turned rope is the indicator (ours, untested).

words: water; swim; float; life jacket; grown-up; pool; deep
notes: Basic water safety and, where a pool is available, simple swimming: stay with a grown-up, never go near water alone, wear a life jacket on a boat, how to float on the back and kick. The water rules are taught first in health grade 2 (g2-s-outdoor-and-home-safety) and open here as retrieval; PE's days go to the dry-land skills and to understanding basic swimming on dry land for every school (what floating and kicking are and why a back float helps, shown lying on the floor). Assessed by a knowledge task (one safety rule and one swimming idea) and a dry-land skill task for every school (fastening a life jacket and a reach rescue on the floor); in-water tasks (float and kick) only where a pool exists. Teacher note: No child is made to enter water. Any in-water task belongs to the school's own aquatics program, with a qualified lifeguard on site and the school's swim policy.

words: travel; jump; land; balance; roll; weight
notes: Traveling, jumping, landing, balancing and weight shifts in short sequences of three parts in a circuit, with changes of speed and direction. Assessed by a skill task: a three-part sequence (travel, jump, balance) with a soft landing and a held finish. Adds jog (a slow steady run), first expected in grade 2 in the review tool.

words: bounce; catch; kick; tap; strike; partner
notes: Ball skills used in new settings: bounce to a partner, catch from the bounce, kick to a partner, tap and stop, strike with a hand or a short tool into open space, each in a station. Cues stay on the card, one per station. Assessed by a skill task: one station watched per child on the one cue the child is working on.

words: sequence; beginning; middle; end; pattern; partner
notes: Link three dance moves into a short sequence with a start shape and an end shape, in one dance style and then another. Assessed by a skill task: performs a three-move sequence to the beat. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year.

words: chase; flee; dodge; fake; space; tag
notes: Name basic tactics for chasing and fleeing games: dodge, change direction, use open space, make a fake. Introduces the game-tactics question: where is the space, and what is my best move? Strategies and tactics are first expected in grade 3 (from the tool), so this row stays at naming in play, no scoring. Assessed by a knowledge task: names one move for the chaser and one for the fleer. Teacher note: tag with no elimination; a tagged child does a task and rejoins.

words: level; pathway; speed; direction; shape
notes: Show understanding of traveling, in-place and object-handling skills while moving: perform a movement and name the idea (move at a low level, throw along a straight path). Assessed by a knowledge task shown while moving and said in one short sentence.

words: stretch; warm up; cool down; muscle; slowly
notes: Say why stretching helps before and after exercise: warm muscles stretch better, and slow stretches help the body settle. Warm-up and cool-down start in grade 3 in the tool's tables, so this row only names them. Static stretches come after a warm-up. Assessed by a knowledge task: says one reason to stretch. Teacher note: no bouncing, stretch only to a gentle pull.

words: energy; fruit; vegetable; water; snack; drink
notes: Pick foods and drinks that give energy for activity and name water as the drink for moving. Taught from foods a class commonly sees and never about body size. Health grade 2 teaches foods that give energy for play first (g2-fn-pick-best-snack, health K to 2 unit 12); PE opens with it as retrieval and teaches choosing what to eat and drink before and while playing and the water break, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task: sorts a picture set into 'gives energy for play'. Teacher note: no body talk; food allergies respected.

words: rule; fair; safe; turn; choose; same
notes: Explain how following rules keeps everyone safe and treats people fairly, and with teacher guidance make fair choices (who goes first, how to share). Assessed by a knowledge task and conduct: says why a rule helps and follows it in a game.

words: problem; fix; idea; listen; solve; sorry
notes: With teacher help, talk over a problem in an activity and suggest fixes. Introduces team talk as four steps a child can say: stop, say what happened, listen, find a fair way (the same words as health's conflict steps, g2-v-settle-it-with-words, so a child meets one set), then try it. Assessed by conduct: uses the steps in a role-played or real problem.

words: goal; try; practice; check; reach; soon
notes: Make a clear goal that can be seen and reached soon (ten jumps in a row, three catches), practice, and check. Introduces the goal cycle: pick, practice, check. Assessed by a knowledge task: says the goal, and shows the check. Goals are the child's own and private.

words: hard; tricky; practice; remember; matter
notes: Notice personal difficulties that come up while moving (a hard skill, a fear of the ball) and look back on a PE experience to say why it mattered. Uses the calm-steps card when a task is hard. Assessed by a knowledge task: names a hard moment and one thing that helped.

words: jump; land; balance; stable; base; counterbalance
notes: Jump and land while staying in place (two feet, one foot, a half turn) and balance on different body parts, including a partner balance at a safe size. Cues: bend, swing, land soft, hold. Boundary: in place, stable surfaces. Assessed by a skill task: lands three jumps softly and holds two balances for three counts. Teacher note: soft floor or mats; partner balances stay low.

words: roll; log roll; forward roll; tuck; curl; mat
notes: Body rolls in a fixed spot on a mat: log roll, egg roll, and a forward roll down an incline for children who are ready. Cues: tuck chin, round back, hands on the mat. Assessed by a skill task: one roll watched against two cues; rolls that need more tries are adapted, not skipped. Teacher note: mats; no rolling for a child with a neck or back concern from a family or nurse; a log roll is always the alternative.

words: rope; jump; tricks; rhythm; endurance; partner
notes: Jump rope through several tasks: self-turned forward and backward, with a step and a jump, a long rope with a turner, a partner rope. Cues: small jumps, turn from the wrists, steady beat. Assessed by a skill task: ten jumps in a row at the child's own pace; growth is measured against the child's own start. Teacher note: adapted ropes for a range of ability.

words: throw; roll; catch; underhand; overhand; target; fingers
notes: Roll from a fixed spot (a ball to a target), throw overhand and underhand in several tasks (to a wall, a hoop, a partner), and catch at several heights. Cues: step, throw, follow through; hands out, eyes on it, soft hands. Passing with the hands to a moving partner is owned in grade 4. Assessed by a skill task: throws three of five to a target at a set distance with the cues, catches three of five tosses. Teacher note: one throwing direction; no human targets.

words: bat; racket; paddle; stroke; swing; contact
notes: Hit with a long-handled tool (bat, hockey stick) and a short-handled tool (paddle, racket) in several tasks: off a tee, a toss to oneself, a gentle toss from a partner. Cues: side to the target, eyes on the ball, swing through. Assessed by a skill task: contacts a gently tossed ball three of five times with a swing through. Teacher note: swing space cleared; one batter per space; line behind a safe distance.

words: laces; kick; dribble; tap; control; pass
notes: Kick with the laces to a target and to a partner and dribble with the feet in open space, changing direction. Cues: plant foot beside the ball, laces through the ball, small taps. Assessed by a skill task: kicks a rolled ball to a partner and dribbles through five cones without bumping. Teacher note: kicks aimed at a wall or goal, never at a person.

words: dribble; bounce; control; finger pads; walk; move
notes: Bounce a ball with the hands in place and on the move with one hand, then with a changed hand. Cues: push, fingers wide, eyes up. Boundary: dribbling with the ball while changing direction against defenders is later. Assessed by a skill task: dribbles ten steps without losing the ball.

words: step; hop; pattern; four counts; phrase; partner
notes: Dance steps strung into short phrases in two dance styles (a folk dance, a line dance): four-count patterns in a line, a circle or with a partner. Works toward the traveling chain and the dance sequence owned in grade 4. Assessed by a skill task: performs a four-count pattern to the beat. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: safe; space; dodge; change; direction; awareness
notes: Use movement ideas and tactics to stay safe where the setting keeps changing: scan the room, keep eyes up, choose open space, change direction, use the safe-space bubble. Practiced in small dodge and tag games with no elimination. Assessed by a knowledge task: names a safe move when the setting changes.

words: warm up; cool down; dynamic; static; muscle; slow
notes: Tell when a warm-up and cool-down are needed for different activities and name one of each (a walk then arm swings, then slow stretches). Warm-up and cool-down start in grade 3 in the tool's tables (from the tool). Assessed by a knowledge task: says when a warm-up is needed and picks a fitting one. Teacher note: stretch after a warm-up, never cold; no bouncing.

words: key part; cue; correct; form; pattern
notes: Name the key parts of a skill done correctly (for a throw: side to the target, step opposite foot, follow through), and tell what a skill looks like when it is done correctly. Builds on cue-words from kindergarten. Assessed by a knowledge task: names the parts of one skill and finds a part in a partner's try.

words: endurance; strength; flexibility; muscle; heart
notes: Describe with examples activities that build the health-related fitness parts: endurance (the heart and lungs), muscle strength, muscle endurance and flexibility. Introduces the fitness parts as a chart used all the way through. Assessed by a knowledge task: matches an activity to a part. Body composition is not taught as a body measure. Teacher note: no weighing, no body measurements.

words: benefit; healthy; sleep; mood; strong; energy
notes: Describe the benefits of being physically active: a stronger heart and bones, better sleep, a better mood, more energy. The handoff skips grade 2 because the heart idea returns here after a pause; grade 2 holds it in warm-up and cool-down talk. Assessed by a knowledge task: names two benefits.

words: kind; include; group; team; invite; support
notes: Act kindly so group activity stays positive: invite someone in, pass to everyone, use encouraging words, and use team talk when a group is stuck. Assessed by conduct against stated behaviors in group tasks.

words: safe; reminder; careful; equipment; alone; check
notes: Stay safe on one's own with few reminders: check the space before moving, use equipment correctly, stop on the signal without being asked. Assessed by conduct: the number of reminders needed is a private note for the teacher, never a rank. Teacher note: water breaks in warm weather; equipment checked before class. Near water: stay with a grown-up and wear a life jacket on a boat.

words: express; benefit; health; mood; favorite; creative
notes: Describe how favorite activities let a child express themselves and explain the health benefits of moving (heart, bones, mood). Assessed by a knowledge task: one sentence for expression and one for health.

words: outside; recess; walk; after school; weekend; family
notes: Find ways to be active outside PE class: recess games, walking, family play, a park, a home activity with nothing to buy. Each child picks one and tries it for a week using the goal cycle. Assessed by a knowledge task: names one and when it will happen. The health course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year.

words: calm; breathe; count; stretch; favorite; works for me
notes: Name which calming methods work best during activity (slow breath, counting, a drink of water, stepping out for a minute with a role) and use one. Assessed by a knowledge task: names the best method and uses it in a game. Teacher note on emotions: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: chain; pathway; level; speed; link; smooth
notes: Join different traveling movements into a chain over several tasks (run, leap, roll, balance) with smooth links and a changed speed or direction between them. Cues: smooth link, hold the finish. Assessed by a skill task: a four-part chain with smooth links. Teacher note: soft landing area.

words: weight; hands; wrist; arms; bridge
notes: Move weight from the feet onto the hands and back while staying in place (a bunny hop, a donkey kick, a bear walk to a frog jump). Cues: hands shoulder-width, look at the hands, push through the shoulders. Assessed by a skill task: moves weight to hands and back with control. Teacher note: mats; no inverted balances; a spotter's role is for a stable bridge only.

words: sequence; jump; roll; balance; start shape; end shape
notes: Join jumps, rolls, balances and feet-to-hands shifts into one in-place sequence with a clear start shape and end shape. Assessed by a skill task: a five-part sequence performed twice, once for a baseline and once at the check.

words: sequence; phrase; style; folk; line; partner
notes: Link traveling, in-place and object-handling moves into a sequence in several dance styles (a line dance, a folk dance, a scarf or ribbon routine), with a beginning, a middle and an end. Assessed by a skill task: performs a sequence to the beat. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: volley; bump; set; overhead; underhand; waist
notes: Hit with the hands above waist level (overhead volley, set) and below waist level (underhand bump, underhand strike) with a light ball, in several tasks alone, against a wall and with a partner. Cues: get under it, hands together, push up. Overhead volleying starts in grade 4 (from the tool). Assessed by a skill task: three volleys in a row with a partner. Teacher note: light ball for wrists.

words: serve; underhand; toss; contact; target; net
notes: Serve an object from a fixed spot: an underhand serve with a hand or paddle into an open area over a low net or line. Cues: step, swing low, contact. Assessed by a skill task: three of five serves into the target area.

words: pass; chest pass; bounce pass; receive; partner; gather
notes: Pass an object with hands or feet to a partner and gather it, in several tasks while standing still and then moving a few steps. Cues: step to the partner, aim at the chest, soft hands to receive. Passing with hands while moving starts in grade 4 (from the tool). Assessed by a skill task: five passes in a row in a pair.

words: dribble; pass; shoot; target; goal; combine
notes: Combine handling an object with moving to send it at a target (dribble then shoot, catch then throw, dribble with the feet then pass), in several tasks. Cues: eyes up, move then send. Assessed by a skill task: dribble-and-send at a target. Teacher note: targets are a goal, hoop or wall, never a person.

words: attack; space; pass; open; invade; goal
notes: Explain how to attack in small-group play where teams move into the other team's area: spread out, pass to open players, move to space. Uses the game-tactics question (where is the space?). Small-sided play of three on three, no elimination. Assessed by a knowledge task: names two attacking moves in a game picture.

words: force; follow through; aim; angle; speed; stable base
notes: Understand which movement ideas make object-handling skills work well: step with the opposite foot, follow through, aim at the target, bend the knees for balance. Assessed by a knowledge task: says why a cue helps a throw.

words: agility; balance; coordination; power; reaction time; speed
notes: Describe and show activities that build the skill-related fitness parts: agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time and speed. Added to the fitness parts chart. Assessed by a knowledge task and a skill task: matches an activity to a part and shows one. No fitness scores are used for grades.

words: pulse; neck; wrist; beat; breathing; sweat
cross_subject: science:4-LS1-1 (body structures and what they do)
notes: Find the pulse at the wrist or neck and count it for ten seconds at rest and after activity, name activities that raise the heart rate, and notice and describe how activity changes the body. Children match the count to a face on the effort scale. Assessed by a knowledge task: finds a pulse and says what changed. Teacher note: counts are private and never compared; a child who cannot find a pulse can use a hand on the chest.

words: level; pathway; shape; rhythm; space; effort
notes: Use movement ideas (level, pathway, effort, shape) in dance, gymnastics, rhythms and individual activities, and name them. Assessed by a knowledge task: names the idea used in a routine.

words: role; view; agree; decide; fair; plan
notes: Explain how other people see a situation (a player who is left out, a slower player), and talk with others to decide who does what in an activity. Assessed by conduct: takes a role and decides with the group using team talk.

words: country; culture; tradition; game; dance; people
notes: Take part in movement activities from cultures around the world (a game, a dance), describe each one and name the culture it comes from. The handoff skips grades 2 and 3 because world games stay in dance and game units; this row returns to them with the culture named. Assessed by a knowledge task: describes an activity and names where it comes from. Each cultural claim is sourced before a unit says it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: connect; friend; group; difficulty; together
notes: Describe how favorite activities connect a child with others, and spot difficulties a group faces when moving together (too little space, uneven skill, one dominating). Assessed by a knowledge task: names one connection and one group difficulty with a fix.

words: reason; interest; strength; grow; practice
notes: Give reasons for the activities picked based on interests, and name movement strengths and where to practice to grow. Assessed by a knowledge task: one strength, one thing to practice, one reason for an activity.

words: swim; float; stroke; rescue; reach; throw
notes: Basic water safety and, where a pool is available, simple swimming: float, a front and back kick, reach or throw rescue without going in, and the buddy rule. The handoff skips grades 3 and 4 because water safety returns in grade 5 units by a pool or by a floor-based version. Assessed by a knowledge task (rescue steps and rules) and a dry-land skill task for every school: a reach rescue, a throw rescue to a target and fastening a life jacket; in-water tasks only where a pool exists. Teacher note: No child is made to enter water. Any in-water task belongs to the school's own aquatics program, with a qualified lifeguard on site and the school's swim policy.

words: pass; dribble; shoot; space; goal; small-sided
notes: Passing, dribbling with the hands and feet, and sending to a target used in three-on-three invasion games (a soccer or basketball-style game with no elimination). Cues on the card, the tactics question asked each game. Assessed by a skill task and conduct. Teacher note: games have fair teams chosen privately; no public picking.

words: serve; volley; rally; net; wall; court
notes: Serving, volleying and short-tool strikes used in a net or wall game with a low net, played one-on-one or two-on-two. Assessed by a skill task: a three-hit rally.

words: bat; field; throw; catch; base; run
notes: Throwing, catching and striking used in a striking and fielding game with a tee or a gentle pitch: hit, run to a base, field, throw. The handoff from grade 3 skips grade 4 because striking returns here in a game setting. Assessed by a skill task: throws and catches in a fielding task. Teacher note: batting space cleared; soft balls.

words: routine; sequence; rope; chain; style; partner
notes: Chains, in-place sequences, dance sequences and jump-rope routines used in a longer routine of eight parts, alone or with a partner, with the rope appearing in a circuit. The grade 3 rope handoff skips a grade because rope returns here in the routine. Assessed by a skill task: performs the routine twice.

words: defend; mark; guard; block; space; goal
notes: Explain how to defend in small-group play where teams move into the other team's area: stay between the player and the goal, close the space, keep eyes on the ball. Assessed by a knowledge task: names two defending moves in a game picture.

words: problem; idea; test; change; rule; plan
notes: Show ways of solving problems that come up in games and activities: stop, name the problem, offer two ideas, test one. Practiced as a game rule change the class proposes and tests. Assessed by a knowledge task: names a problem and a test.

words: frequency; intensity; time; type; plan; improve
notes: Describe how frequency, intensity, time and type (FITT) improve a skill or fitness: how often, how hard, how long and what kind. Introduces the FITT plan, used from here to grade 12. Assessed by a knowledge task: changes one FITT part in a plan and says why. No fitness scores are used for grades. Fitness records are kept privately by the student.

words: technology; counter; timer; video; app; track
notes: Name technology that can help meet activity goals (a step counter, a timer, a video of a skill) and what each can and cannot show. Assessed by a knowledge task: names one tool and one limit. Teacher note: personal data stays private; devices are never required.

words: energy; hydrate; water; carbohydrate; protein; snack
notes: Explain how what is eaten and drunk affects activity: water before and after, energy foods before long activity, a snack to recover. The handoff from grade 2 skips grades because food and drink return here with fitness work. The health course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task. Teacher note: no body talk, no diets; allergies respected.

words: disagree; compromise; solve; team; calm; agree
notes: Work through problems alone, with a partner or in a small team: a disagreement over a rule or a call, using calm steps and team talk. Assessed by conduct: resolves a disagreement in a role play or real game.

words: fair; custom; rule; honest; referee; call
notes: Make fair decisions that fit the customs of the activity: self-officiate a small game, play by honor calls, and follow the activity's own customs (a bow in a martial form, a handshake in a net game). Assessed by conduct: self-officiates a game. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: goal; baseline; progress; record; reach; checkpoint
cross_subject: math:5.G.A.2 (a line graph of the child own scores over weeks)
notes: Set visible goals for a longer stretch of time (four to six weeks) for fitness or a skill, with a baseline, a check each week and a graph or chart of progress, kept privately. Owns both the fitness goal indicator and the longer-goal indicator. Assessed by a knowledge task: a goal with a baseline and a check. Fitness data stays with the child; no comparing, no ranking, no use as a grade. Where math has not yet taught 5.G.A.2 (math grade 5 unit 10, days 135 to 149), the child charts the weekly checks as a scaled bar graph (3.MD.B.3).

words: review; remember; matter; proud; learn; change
notes: Review PE experiences to understand what they mean to the child: a unit scrapbook, a best moment, a hard moment and what the calm steps did. Assessed by a knowledge task: one sentence on what the unit meant.

words: sequence; style; transition; tempo; formation; counts
notes: Do movement sequences in a range of dance styles (a social dance, a line dance, a cultural dance, a rhythmic routine): eight-count phrases, transitions, and a sequence of four phrases. Cues: count, level, transition. Assessed by a skill task: performs a four-phrase sequence to the beat. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: technique; form; repetition; set; core; posture
notes: Use sound technique in health-building fitness activities: a body-weight squat, a push-up on knees or toes, a plank, a jog with posture, a stretch held ten seconds after a warm-up. Cues: neutral spine, controlled speed, breathe. Assessed by a skill task: one exercise from each fitness part with the cue. Teacher note: stop for sharp pain; no max lifts; exercise is never a punishment.

words: agility; power; reaction; ladder; balance; coordination
notes: Use sound technique in exercises that build skill-related fitness: an agility ladder, a hop and balance sequence, a reaction drill with a partner, a power jump with no equipment. Cues: quick feet, soft landing, eyes up. Assessed by a skill task: demonstrates one drill with the cue. Teacher note: soft floor, clear space.

words: sidearm; underhand; overhand; roll; accuracy; follow through
notes: Roll and throw underhand, sidearm and overhand with good form in drills and modified target games (a target ball game, a bowling-style roll game). Cues: eyes on target, step opposite foot, rotate the hips, follow through. Assessed by a skill task: two forms, three of five on target. Teacher note: one throwing direction; no human targets.

words: catch; give; gear; glove; absorb; ready position
notes: Catch with good form, with or without gear (a glove or a scoop), in drills and small-sided games: ready hands, eyes on the ball, give with the catch. Assessed by a skill task: catches a tossed ball at three heights. Teacher note: ball sized for the group; no catching a hard ball bare-handed.

words: pass; receive; lead pass; cut; target; timing
notes: Pass and receive while moving in small-sided games: lead the receiver, move to an open spot, receive on the move. Assessed by a skill task: five passes on the move in a three-on-three drill.

words: dribble; control; protect; change of pace; speed dribble; head up
notes: Use a dribbling skill (hands or feet) in drills and small-sided games: control while traveling, change of direction, head up. Assessed by a skill task: dribbles through cones and past a passive defender.

words: stance; ready position; shuffle; mark; guard
notes: Get into a ready defensive position in drills and small games: knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet, hands out, between the player and the goal. Assessed by a skill task: holds the stance and shuffles side to side.

words: serve; forehand; backhand; stroke; swing; rally
notes: Works toward the striking and net skills owned in grade 7: a handheld forehand, a swing at a tossed ball, an underhand serve with a short tool. Boundary: modified rallies, low net, light equipment. Assessed by a skill task: contacts a tossed ball with a swing.

words: space; time; force; balance; flow; changing setting
notes: Name how to use movement ideas well when the setting keeps changing: space, time, force, balance, in an obstacle course, a tag game and a small-sided game. Assessed by a knowledge task: names the idea used to solve a movement problem.

words: health-related; skill-related; endurance; flexibility; agility; reaction time
notes: Name the health-related and skill-related fitness parts and tell them apart: health-related fitness protects health, skill-related fitness helps in sport. Sorting tasks and one drill per part. Assessed by a knowledge task: sorts ten activities.

words: dynamic; static; warm-up; cool-down; range of motion; hold
notes: Use dynamic stretches in warm-ups and static stretches in cool-downs and training: leg swings and lunges before, a held stretch after. Assessed by a knowledge task: builds a warm-up and cool-down. Teacher note: no bouncing, no pain.

words: heart rate; beats per minute; resting; target zone; aerobic
cross_subject: math:6.RP.A.3 (a ten-second count scaled to a minute)
notes: Understand heart rate and what it shows about aerobic fitness: resting and working rates, beats per minute from a ten- or fifteen-second count, how the rate drops with fitness over weeks. The handoff skips grade 5 because pulse work continues inside the fitness and goal rows there. Assessed by a knowledge task: counts, converts and says what it shows. Teacher note: counts are private; no heart-rate score is a grade; a child with a heart or breathing condition follows the nurse's and family's guidance. Times six is multiplication from earlier grades; ratio language comes with the grade 6 ratio unit.

words: lifetime; options; community; access; recreation; interest
notes: List ways to stay active (team sports, individual sports, dance, outdoor, community programs, active transport), with ones that fit different interests, budgets and abilities. Assessed by a knowledge task: a personal list of five ways with how to find each. Returns to g4-reasons-strengths after a skip: reasons to move come back here.

words: analyze; phase; preparation; execution; follow through; compare
notes: Break a skill into its key parts to analyze how it is done: preparation, action, follow through; watch a partner or a video and name which part to fix. Introduces skill analysis, which carries the cue words forward. The handoff skips grade 5 because key parts return here in analysis. Assessed by a knowledge task: names a part to fix and the cue to fix it. Taught in the first section of the grade; the motor rows then use the analysis words.

words: respect; difference; inclusive; contribute; teammate; ability
notes: Understand and welcome differences among classmates in activities (ability, size, background, language) and show care for others by contributing helpfully to a team. Assessed by conduct against stated behaviors in team tasks. Teacher note: no public team picking; groups are made privately by the teacher.

words: rule; safe; equipment; behavior; responsible; check
notes: Follow game rules in different movement settings, and name and practice safe, suitable behavior during activity and with equipment. The grade 3 safety handoff returns in more complex settings. Assessed by conduct: follows rules and equipment steps in two settings. Teacher note: equipment checked before class; water in warm weather. The buddy rule and what to do near water.

words: self-expression; variety; engaged; health; challenge
notes: Explain how self-expression affects how involved a person gets in activity, and take part in many kinds of activity that improve health (a dance unit, a fitness unit, a team game). Assessed by a knowledge task and conduct: joins several kinds and says which fits best.

words: grip; stance; rotation; contact; follow through; level swing
notes: Swing a long-handled tool to hit, with a mature pattern: grip, side stance, weight shift, hip rotation, contact, follow through. Used with a bat, a hockey stick or a golf-style club on a tee or a tossed ball. Assessed by a skill task: contacts a tossed ball with a mature pattern, three of five. Teacher note: swing space cleared; one swinger per space.

words: self-toss; open space; placement; direction; strike; field
notes: Strike a self-dropped or tossed ball with a tool into open space in drills and small games, choosing a place to hit. Assessed by a skill task: places a hit to a named zone.

words: accuracy; distance; power; velocity; rotation; target
notes: Throw with accuracy, distance and power in drills and small-sided games: a throw to a target, a long throw, a throw to a base. Cues: hips then shoulders then arm, step toward the target. Assessed by a skill task and a knowledge task: one throw each way, and which cue gives the power. Teacher note: warm up the arm first; one throwing direction.

words: underhand serve; overhand serve; toss; contact; placement
notes: Hit a serve with the hand (underhand and overhand) and with a short or long tool (underhand, overhand) in drills and modified net and wall games. Assessed by a skill task: five serves into the court area, to a named zone.

words: forehand; backhand; ready position; swing; rally; placement
notes: Hit forehand and backhand strokes with a short or long tool in drills and modified games: ready stance, turn, swing, recover. Assessed by a skill task: a rally of three strokes alone and against a partner.

words: volley; shoot; open; cut; dribble; screen
notes: Works toward the skills owned in grade 8: a volley against a wall, a stick dribble, a shot at a goal, a cut to get open. Assessed by a skill task: one watched try of each.

words: circuit; routine; form; hiking; orienteering; pace
notes: Fitness, dance and an outdoor activity (a hike, an orienteering course, a field walk) used as settings for form: form is checked in a circuit, a routine and a walk with a map and pace. Assessed by a skill task: form kept in a circuit of six stations. Teacher note: weather, route and water checked first; stay in groups.

words: create space; spread; cut; screen; support; width
notes: Explain attacking moves that create space in invasion games: spread out, move without the ball, make a cut, pass and move. Assessed by a knowledge task: names two moves and points to the space on a diagram.

words: close space; mark; zone; person-to-person; block; transition
notes: Explain defending moves that close space and block opponents in invasion games: person-to-person and zone, closing down, staying goal-side. Assessed by a knowledge task: picks a defense for a diagram and says why.

words: canon; unison; contrast; form; tempo; space
notes: Use movement ideas (space, time, force, relationship) to change up different dance and rhythm forms: a unison section, a canon, a contrast. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task: changes a sequence with one idea and says which.

words: progression; overload; specificity; reversibility; FITT
notes: Use FITT, progression, overload and specificity across different activities: how to raise an activity a little at a time, why the plan must match the goal. Assessed by a knowledge task: changes a plan for a different goal and explains why. Teacher note: no maximum tests; increases stay small.

words: aerobic; perceived exertion; talk test; recovery; pace
cross_subject: math:6.RP.A.3 (a rate of effort or pace against time)
notes: Describe how aerobic fitness relates to how hard activity feels: the same pace feels easier as fitness grows. Uses the effort scale as a one-to-ten scale and the talk test. Assessed by a knowledge task: rates effort at three paces and explains the change over weeks. Teacher note: private records, no ranking.

words: agility; power; reaction; coordination; balance; sport
notes: Use what is known about skill-related fitness in different activities: which parts matter most in a sport and how to train them. Assessed by a knowledge task: picks two parts for a sport and a drill for each.

words: rest; recovery; sleep; overtraining; muscle; repair
notes: Analyze how rest changes how the body responds to exercise: recovery days, sleep, and signs of too much. Assessed by a knowledge task: plans rest in a week of activity. Teacher note: rest is not a punishment or a reward.

words: nutrition; hydration; energy; well-being; balance; sleep
cross_subject: science:MS-LS1-3 (body systems work together); science:MS-LS1-7 (food is used for energy)
notes: Describe how eating, exercise and well-being fit together: fuel before and after, water, sleep and mood. The grade 5 food handoff returns here in a wider frame. The health course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task. Teacher note: no body weight, calorie counts, or diet talk.

words: strategy; feedback; positive; specific; plan; teammate
notes: Talk over game plans and strategies with teammates, and give and take useful feedback when the teacher sets it up: one kind comment tied to a cue. Assessed by conduct: gives and takes a specific comment in a peer-watching task.

words: disagree; resolve; opponent; sportsmanship; norm; respect
notes: Settle disagreements with teammates and with opponents using calm steps and team talk, and use and respect the norms of good conduct (shaking hands, honest calls). Assessed by conduct in a self-officiated game. Returns to g5-conflict-solve after a skip: conflict work comes back here in a game setting.

words: social; interest; choice; engaged; motivate; friends
notes: Explain how time with others affects personal involvement in activity, and link choice and interests to how engaged a person becomes. Assessed by a knowledge task: connects a choice to staying involved.

words: frustration; stress; strategy; breathe; reset; self-talk
notes: Use several strategies to manage feelings and behavior during activity: slow breathing, self-talk, a short reset, asking for a role change. Assessed by a knowledge task and conduct: names three strategies and uses one. Teacher note: a child may step out for a reset; it is never a punishment. Returns to g5-review-experiences after a skip: the calm steps come back here. Teacher note on emotions: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: challenge; barrier; group; fear; cost; access
notes: Closely examine challenges faced alone and as a group in movement (fear of failing, cost, space, fitness gap), and test one fix. Assessed by a knowledge task: names a challenge with a fix and tries it.

words: volley; overhead; forearm pass; set; net; rally
notes: Volley with a short or long tool in drills and modified net and wall games: a volley against a wall, over a net, with a paddle or a hand. Cues: ready, contact in front, follow through. Assessed by a skill task: a rally of three volleys with a partner.

words: stick; dribble; carry; control; protect
notes: Dribble an object using a tool (a floor-hockey stick, a lacrosse-style stick) in drills and small games: carry, change direction, protect from a defender. Assessed by a skill task: dribbles around cones and past a passive defender. Teacher note: sticks stay below the knee; goalie gear for shots.

words: shot; goal; aim; release; follow through; power
notes: Shoot at a goal, with or without a tool, in drills and small games: set, aim, release, follow through. Assessed by a skill task: shoots from three spots. Teacher note: goal or hoop target, never a person.

words: cut; fake; screen; get open; V-cut; timing
notes: Use a few different moves to get open while attacking, in drills and small games: a cut, a fake, a change of pace. Assessed by a skill task: gets open for a pass in a three-on-two drill.

words: hike; orienteering; paddle; climb; pace; trail
notes: Use good form in several outdoor activities: hiking with pace and posture, orienteering with a map and compass, paddling a canoe on land first, climbing on a wall or a bar. Teachers pick the activities for the place. Assessed by a skill task: form kept on a course. Teacher note: weather, route, sun, water and ratio checked before going; stay in groups.

words: swim; stroke; rescue; survival; float; hypothermia
notes: Practice water safety and show simple swimming where a pool is available: float, tread, a stroke, a reach rescue, cold-water risks. The handoff skips grades 6 and 7 because water units run in the grades where a pool is available. Assessed by a knowledge task and a dry-land skill task for every school: a reach rescue, a throw rescue to a target and fastening a life jacket; in-water tasks only where a pool exists. Teacher note: No child is made to enter water. Any in-water task belongs to the school's own aquatics program, with a qualified lifeguard on site and the school's swim policy.

words: bat; field; relay; base; run; tag out
notes: Striking, throwing and catching used in a modified striking and fielding game with no elimination: batting, fielding, throwing to a base. Assessed by a skill task and conduct. Returns to g6-catch-form after a skip: catching comes back in fielding.

words: serve; rally; return; court; point; fair
notes: Serves and strokes used in a modified net or wall game: singles and doubles with courtesy calls. Assessed by a skill task: a rally with a serve.

words: pass; dribble; stance; defend; support; transition
notes: Passing, dribbling and defensive stance used in a modified invasion game with four on four, a full-court setting only when space allows. Assessed by a skill task and conduct.

words: routine; circuit; form; sequence; tempo
notes: Dance routines and fitness circuits used to show form in a planned week: sequence, technique, a self-chosen routine. Assessed by a skill task: performs a routine or circuit with correct form.

words: shot selection; placement; angle; weak side; drop; clear
notes: Pick and use the right shot and technique in net and wall games: place away from the opponent, choose a short or deep shot. Assessed by a knowledge task: chooses a shot for a given court picture and says why.

words: gap; infield; outfield; placement; cutoff; hit to space
notes: Explain attacking tactics in striking and fielding games (hit to space, run on contact) and where to place defenders to cover space. Assessed by a knowledge task: places fielders on a diagram.

words: problem; hypothesis; test; adjust; result; evidence
notes: Use problem-solving methods in many games and activities: name the problem, try a change, test it, keep or drop it. Assessed by a knowledge task: records a change and its result.

words: baseline; test; progress; goal; record; retest
cross_subject: math:6.SP.B.4 (a plot of the child own results across weeks)
notes: Choose a personal fitness test (a mile walk or run at a self-set pace, with no time recorded, a push-up count, a sit-and-reach) and use it to track progress toward a goal over a term, privately and by choice. Assessed by a knowledge task: a baseline, a goal and a retest, with a plan change if progress stalls. The student shows the teacher the plan change and the reason, not the numbers. Teacher note: fitness test results are the child's own, never posted, graded or compared; a child may choose a different test.

words: accuracy; privacy; tracker; app; evidence; limit
notes: Judge how useful technology is for reaching activity and fitness goals: accuracy, privacy, cost, and what a tool cannot tell. Assessed by a knowledge task: rates a tool on three points. Teacher note: no tool is required; no personal data is collected by the course.

words: weather; sun; water; map; hike; hydrate
notes: Show understanding of safety steps for the outdoor activities the teacher picks (a hike, an orienteering course, a paddle): weather checks, sun, water, route, buddy rule, what to do when lost. Assessed by a knowledge task: makes a safety checklist for the planned activity. Returns to g6-rules-safe after a skip: the first outdoor day is in grade 7.

words: culture; tradition; meaning; origin; respect; ritual
notes: Explain why an activity matters in a particular culture (a game tied to a festival, a martial art, a traditional dance). The handoff skips grades 5 to 7 because world activities return in dance and game units. The social studies course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task. Each cultural claim is sourced. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: leader; communicate; feedback; teamwork; courtesy; role
notes: Describe how communication, feedback, teamwork and courtesy connect to leading, and lead a small group warm-up or a drill. Assessed by conduct: leads a warm-up for a small group.

words: participation; goal; obstacle; opportunity; schedule; access
notes: Set participation goals based on an honest look at the child's own abilities, and weigh the chances and obstacles for being active outside class (time, cost, transport, weather). Assessed by a knowledge task: a goal, an obstacle and a plan around it.

words: reflect; meaning; change; value; growth; experience
notes: Reflect on PE experiences to see what they mean to the child over the year: a portfolio entry, a best and a hardest moment. Assessed by a knowledge task: a short reflection tied to one unit.

words: lifetime sport; technique; drill; modified game; fundamentals; self-check
notes: Do the key skills of several sports and activities that can last for life, chosen from at least two families (a net or wall sport, a target sport, a striking sport, an invasion game), each in drills and a small game. Assessed by a skill task: key parts of two activities shown and checked against a cue sheet. Years 1 and 2 of the band own the span's indicators across a range of activities (rule 5).

words: recreation; backyard; casual; ultimate; cornhole; badminton; pickleball
notes: Do the key moves of casual recreation and backyard games (flying disc, cornhole, lawn games, badminton, a paddle game) with equipment a family can own cheaply. Assessed by a skill task: key moves of two games, shown and named. Teacher note: sturdy low-cost equipment; space and gear checked.

words: choreography; motif; phrase; form; style; transition
notes: Perform and design movement sequences in one or more dance styles: learn a set sequence, then design a short original phrase with a stated idea. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a skill task: performs a set sequence and a student-designed phrase.

words: aerobic; endurance; pace; cadence; cross-training; stride
notes: Use correct form in endurance (aerobic) training: jogging, cycling or brisk walking, rope, rowing or a dance workout, with posture, stride and breathing. Assessed by a skill task: form kept across a twelve-minute continuous session at the student's own pace. Teacher note: water breaks; own pace; no race.

words: resistance; repetition; set; range of motion; spotting; body weight
notes: Use correct form in strength and muscle endurance training: body-weight and band exercises (squat, push-up, row, lunge, plank) with controlled speed and a full range. Assessed by a skill task: five exercises with form checked against a cue sheet. Teacher note: no max lifts; a trained spotter for any loaded lift.

words: strategy; positioning; tempo; angle; rules; scoring
notes: Show understanding of tactics in the lifetime sports chosen and in casual recreation and backyard games: positioning, shot choice, using the weak side. Assessed by a knowledge task: explains a tactic for each activity and applies it in a game.

words: form; repetition; canon; improvisation; structure; motif
notes: Use movement sequences to create or join in dance forms: a canon, a call and response, a social dance. Returns to g7-dance-ideas after a skip: grade 8 dance is a setting for form, and the canon and contrast ideas come back here. Assessed by a knowledge task and a skill task: names the form and joins one. The dance course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: goal; practice plan; drill; self-check; transfer; feedback
notes: Set a goal for a skill the student chooses and plan practice to reach it: baseline, drills, number of sessions, a peer check and a retest. Assessed by a knowledge task and a skill task: a plan, and the retest against the baseline.

words: overload; specificity; progression; reversibility; individuality; adaptation
notes: Apply exercise principles to the lifelong activities chosen: overload, progression, specificity and reversibility applied to a sport the student picks. The grade 7 handoff returns here with a gap because the principles are used in grade 8 in the test-track row. Assessed by a knowledge task: applies each principle to one activity.

words: target zone; maximum; resting; perceived exertion; interval; recovery
cross_subject: math:6.RP.A.3 (a ten-second count scaled to a minute)
notes: Rate how hard the work feels and adjust effort, and use what is known about heart rate to train safely and build health-related fitness: resting rate, a working zone found from age-based and felt effort, recovery. The handoff from grade 7 skips grade 8 because effort and heart rate work continues in the test-track row. Assessed by a knowledge task: picks a zone for a goal, checks it and adjusts. Teacher note: private records, never graded; a student with a heart or breathing condition follows the nurse's and family's guidance.

words: force; torque; rotation; leverage; momentum; center of mass
cross_subject: science:MS-PS2-2 (a bigger force changes motion more)
notes: Use ideas about force, motion and rotation to check and improve a skill: leverage in a throw or kick, center of mass in a landing, rotation in a swing. The handoff from grade 6 skips years because skill analysis was practiced in motor rows in between and returns here with physics words. Assessed by a knowledge task: analyzes a recorded skill and names a change.

words: courtesy; respect; teamwork; aware; empathy; etiquette
notes: Be aware of how others feel and think during activity, and show courtesy, respect and teamwork. Assessed by conduct against stated behaviors during team tasks.

words: encourage; feedback; coach; observe; specific; peer
notes: Encourage and support others, and offer feedback on others' performance without waiting for the teacher to ask, using a cue sheet. Assessed by conduct: gives specific feedback unprompted in a peer task.

words: choice; interest; challenge level; health; social; expression
notes: Samples activities in many kinds (dance, yoga, aerobics, a sport, an outdoor activity) and records what each one gave: expression, company, health, fit with interests, challenge level. Works toward the choosing indicators owned in grade 10. Assessed by a knowledge task: a one-page activity log kept privately.

words: trail; navigation; paddle; climb; ski; cycle
notes: Do the key moves of a range of outdoor activities the school can offer (hiking, orienteering, paddling, cycling, climbing, snow sports where local): the moves, gear and pace. Assessed by a skill task: key moves of one or two activities. Teacher note: weather, route, helmets and ratio set by the school; stay in groups.

words: flexibility; static; dynamic; range; hold
notes: Use correct technique when stretching to build flexibility: dynamic stretches in warm-ups, static holds after training, held thirty seconds without bouncing. Assessed by a skill task: stretches for six large muscle groups with form. Teacher note: stretch warm muscles only; never to pain.

words: agility; power; plyometric; reaction time; speed; coordination
notes: Use correct technique when training the skill-related fitness parts: agility drills, reaction drills, low plyometrics, balance and coordination work. Assessed by a skill task: a short session with form checked. Teacher note: soft surface; low heights only; volume small. Returns to g8-fitness-dance-apply and g7-skill-fitness-use after a skip: the grade 9 sport rows use these drills.

words: swim; survival; rescue; hypothermia; current; lifeguard
notes: Show water safety and simple swimming where a pool is available: survival float, a stroke, reach and throw rescues, cold-water and current risks, and what to do in an emergency. The handoff skips grade 9 because water units run where a pool exists. Assessed by a knowledge task and a dry-land skill task for every school: a reach rescue, a throw rescue to a target and fastening a life jacket; in-water tasks only where a pool exists. Teacher note: No child is made to enter water. Any in-water task belongs to the school's own aquatics program, with a qualified lifeguard on site and the school's swim policy.

words: route; pace; conditions; risk; navigation; plan
notes: Show understanding of tactics in outdoor activities: route choice, pacing, reading conditions, risk. Assessed by a knowledge task: plans a route or a trip and explains the choices.

words: quality of life; chronic disease; independence; early adulthood; lifestyle
notes: Examine how fitness and health shape quality of life after high school, and discuss the benefits of an active lifestyle in early adulthood. The health course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task: a short written or spoken case.

words: program; endurance; strength; flexibility; schedule; log
notes: Make and follow a plan that mixes endurance, strength and flexibility training for several weeks: FITT per type, a weekly schedule, a log, and a change after a check. Assessed by a knowledge task: the plan, the log and one change. Teacher note: the plan and the log are private and never graded on results.

words: recovery; sleep; rest day; overtraining; periodization
notes: Build rest into a regular activity schedule: rest days, sleep, signs of overtraining. Assessed by a knowledge task: adds rest to the plan and gives the reason. Returns to g7-rest after a skip: rest comes back inside the grade 9 principles row.

words: culture; history; society; tradition; identity; sport
notes: Discuss how games, sports and dance have shaped societies and cultures over time, and examine how one activity is valued in different cultures. The handoff skips grade 9 because culture work returns with the social studies course here. The social studies course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task: a short case on one activity in two cultures. Cultural claims are sourced. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: wearable; data; privacy; accuracy; app; evidence
notes: Examine and use technology that supports an active, healthy life: pick a tool, use it for two weeks, and judge what it showed. The handoff skips grade 9 because the technology judgment of grade 8 returns here with a tool in use. Assessed by a knowledge task. Teacher note: no tool is required; no data leaves the student.

words: fuel; hydration; recovery; supplement; protein; performance
notes: Name foods that help or hurt performance, recovery and enjoyment of activity: water, timing of meals, and the limits of supplements and drinks. The handoff skips grades 8 and 9 because food and drink stay with the health course in those years. The health course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task. Teacher note: no body weight or calorie talk.

words: injury; sun; hydrate; equipment; space; protect
notes: Follow safe habits: prevent injury, give space, drink water, care for gear, follow rules, protect skin from sun. The handoff from grade 8 skips grade 9 because the safety checklist returns here in outdoor and gear-based settings. Assessed by conduct: follows a stated safety checklist during an outdoor or gear-based activity.

words: leader; challenge; teamwork; decision; evaluate; role
notes: Reason through challenges alone and in teams during activity, and judge how well leadership works in different activity settings (a team captain, a coach, a peer leader). Assessed by conduct and a knowledge task: leads a task and evaluates the leadership.

standard: SHAPE.S4.12.1; SHAPE.S4.12.2; SHAPE.S4.12.3; SHAPE.S4.12.4; SHAPE.S4.12.5; SHAPE.S4.12.6; SHAPE.S4.12.7; SHAPE.S4.12.8; SHAPE.S4.12.9
words: choice; calm; emotion; challenge; interest
notes: The personal plan in short form, so every student meets the choice indicators in the two required years (Cory, 2026-11-20), with every part of each taught: picks and tries a different activity each term with a stated reason, among them one that lets the student express themselves (a dance, yoga or aerobics) and one with time with others; says how each fits health, interests and challenge level, and does well at a fitting level; sets movement goals tied to their own interests; looks at what affects staying active after high school (life choices, money, motivation, access); uses a chosen way to manage emotions during activity; and thinks over what PE has meant to them. Grades 11 and 12, the electives, deepen the plan. Assessed by a knowledge task (the log of choices and reasons, and a one-page plan to stay active after school with its goals and what may get in the way, ending in a short reflection) and by conduct (a chosen way to manage emotions used in a hard moment). Teacher note on emotions: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: chosen activity; technique; plan; refine; self-coach
notes: Applies the key skills of a lifetime sport, a casual game, an outdoor activity or a dance chosen by the student, with a technique check against a cue sheet. Grades 11 and 12 carry the motor indicators of the span. Assessed by a skill task in the chosen activity.

words: form; session; progression; warm-up; cool-down
notes: Applies correct form in aerobic, strength, flexibility and skill-related training inside the student's own program. Assessed by a skill task: a full session with form checked. Teacher note: no max lifts; trained spotter for loaded lifts.

words: program; goal; principle; log; adjust; plan
notes: Applies exercise principles in the student's own program for a term, with a goal, a log and a mid-term change. Assessed by a knowledge task: the plan and a log summary. Logs and ratings are the student's own and private; they are never graded on results.

words: zone; effort; recovery; heart rate; rest
notes: Trains by effort and heart rate and builds rest in: zone choice by goal, an interval session, a recovery day. Assessed by a knowledge task: a session plan with effort ratings. Logs and ratings are the student's own and private; they are never graded on results.

words: tactics; conditions; strategy; scouting; adapt; choose
notes: Applies tactics in the student's chosen sport, casual game or outdoor activity in a longer game or trip. Assessed by a knowledge task: explains tactics used in a recorded game or a trip log.

words: lead; mentor; coach; peer feedback; encourage
notes: Leads a small group in a skill or fitness session and gives unprompted, specific feedback. Assessed by conduct and a knowledge task: leads a session with a plan.

words: safety; protect; respect; etiquette; space; gear
notes: Applies safe habits and courtesy as the usual way of acting in new activities, with students setting their own safety checklist. Assessed by conduct against the checklist.

words: express; yoga; aerobics; dance; company; club
notes: Choose and join activities, such as dance, yoga or aerobics, that let a student express themselves, and choose activities that offer time with others (a class, a club, a team). Assessed by a knowledge task and conduct: a chosen activity joined for a term with a reason. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.

words: health; interest; match; routine; habit; motivation
notes: Find and join an activity that improves health and one that matches interests, and explain the match. Assessed by a knowledge task: a short written reason for each choice. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.

words: challenge; success; level; skill; adapt; stretch
notes: Choose activity at a fitting challenge level and do well in it: pick a level from a range, adjust when too easy or hard. Assessed by a knowledge task and a skill task: a chosen level and a record of success. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.

words: lifelong; technique; refine; self-coach; independent
notes: Applies motor skills in activities the student will keep after school, with a self-written technique check. Assessed by a skill task in a chosen activity. New in grade 12: the student writes the cue sheet and coaches a partner.

words: form; safety; program; session; coaching
notes: Applies correct form across training types in the student's own long-term program. Assessed by a skill task: a session coached by a partner. New in grade 12: a session the student designs and a partner coaches.

words: program; goal; progression; recovery; log; review
notes: Designs and follows a full program for a term with a goal, FITT per type, heart-rate or effort checks and rest, and reviews it. Assessed by a knowledge task: the program and a review. Teacher note: private records; no graded results.

words: adult life; quality of life; technology; food; routine; sleep
notes: Plans an active week for early adulthood (work, study or a trade) with tools and food that support it. The health course units must name this row when they are written, so the same thing is not taught twice in a year. Assessed by a knowledge task: a one-week plan. Teacher note: no body weight or calorie talk.

words: lead; organize; feedback; evaluate; event; team
notes: Leads or organizes a small activity event (a class game day, a skills clinic), gives feedback and evaluates the leadership. Assessed by conduct and a knowledge task: the event plan and an evaluation. New in grade 12: the student organizes an event, not a single session.

words: community; culture; respect; inclusion; access; volunteer
notes: Applies courtesy and care in community-style activity and examines how a chosen activity is valued in other cultures. Assessed by conduct and a knowledge task: a short community activity case. Each cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Sacred or ceremonial activities: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground.

words: goal; interest; plan; milestone; review; motivation
notes: Create and build movement goals tied to the student's interests, with milestones and a review. Assessed by a knowledge task: a goal plan with milestones. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.

words: life choices; money; motivation; access; community; barrier
notes: Study what affects staying active after high school: work and study, money, motivation, access and local options. Assessed by a knowledge task: a plan around two barriers. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.

words: stress; emotion; strategy; regulation; exercise; reset
notes: Examine and use chosen ways to manage emotions during activity (breath work, pacing, a break, movement for stress). Assessed by a knowledge task and conduct: a chosen method used in a hard moment. Teacher note on emotions: APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground. Returns to g10-choose-active-apply after a skip: the strategies are practised inside the chosen-activity rows in grade 11. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.

words: reflect; meaning; value; portfolio; growth; experience
notes: Think over PE experiences across the years to understand what they mean to the student, as a portfolio piece. Assessed by a knowledge task: a reflection with two examples. An elective year: deepens the grade 10 plan; the indicator is owned in grade 10.
